+---

+title: Rebalance the Swift prompt rules for the toolchain gate
+---
+## What
+
+The move to `swift format` changes which bullets a tool owns. One requirement takes one owner, thus each bullet must move to the correct side. Do the task "Move idioms-swift to the toolchain swift format" first, because its measurements decide two rows here.
+
+Files to change:
+- `builtin/validators/swift/rules/value-semantics.md`
+- `builtin/validators/swift/rules/idioms.md`
+- `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/rules/idioms-swift.md` — the `supersedes` key and the body section that states why it supersedes nothing
+- `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs`
+
+**One bullet comes BACK to the prompt.** The toolchain has no rule like `preferFinalClasses`. The bullet "mark classes `final`" came out of `value-semantics.md` when the swiftformat gate took it. No tool decides it now, thus write it back into `value-semantics.md`.
+
+**Four bullets leave the prompt.** The toolchain decides every bullet `idioms.md` still states:
+
+| the bullet of `idioms.md` | the toolchain rule that takes it |
+|---|---|
+| empty-collection variables use a literal | `AlwaysUseLiteralForEmptyCollectionInit` |
+| omit the return clause when it is `Void` | `NoVoidReturnOnFunctionSignature` |
+| do not repeat the type name in a static member | `DontRepeatTypeInStaticProperties` |
+| a loop that filters says `where` | `UseWhereClausesInForLoops` |
+
+The first bullet holds a long note about SwiftFormat's `propertyTypes` rule and `--property-types inferred`. Delete that note. The toolchain decides this bullet in the correct direction, thus the warning is not true any more.
+
+**If `idioms.md` then states no bullet, delete the file** and make `idioms-swift` state `supersedes: idioms`. Rewrite the body section "Why this rule supersedes nothing" to state what the rule now supersedes.
+
+**One row waits for a measurement.** The `where` bullet names two DON'Ts. If `UseWhereClausesInForLoops` does not report `things.filter { $0 > 2 }.forEach { thing in print(thing) }`, that half stays in `idioms.md`, the file is not empty, and `idioms-swift` supersedes nothing. The task above measures this. Read its answer before you delete the file.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `value-semantics.md` states the `final` bullet again, with a DO and a DON'T.
+- [ ] `idioms.md` states no bullet that a toolchain rule decides.
+- [ ] `idioms.md` states nothing about `propertyTypes` or `--property-types`.
+- [ ] The `supersedes` key of `idioms-swift` agrees with what `idioms.md` holds: it names `idioms` if the file is gone, and it names nothing if the file keeps the `where` half.
+- [ ] No bullet has two owners. No bullet has no owner.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Update `the_shipped_swift_idioms_tool_rule_owns_each_bullet_it_took` in `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs` for the new set of taken bullets.
+- [ ] Write a test that holds `value-semantics.md` to stating the `final` bullet, and holds the gate silent on a class that is not `final`. A bullet deleted again fails the test by name.
+- [ ] Write a test that holds `idioms.md` to naming `propertyTypes` nowhere.
+- [ ] Run `cargo test -p swissarmyhammer-validators swift`. Every test passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the failing tests first, then write the code that makes them pass. #swift
\ No newline at end of file
